meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_56_packages.json, all reference===56 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_56.txt (98 lines). For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, נִקְרָא used as identity statements) were considered for addition. Concepts that are purely eitza (causal, 'על ידי') or are verse-proof citations rather than conceptual equivalences were excluded.

However, this is a biblical phrase (Deut. 16:3) that serves as a proof-text rather than the Rebbe establishing a new conceptual equivalence. The connection is: מצה = machloket = daat (already in dataset via edge 1764 + edge 1769-related cluster). Adding לחם עני as a separate node would not enrich the graph meaningfully.

The sighing (אנחה) is described as eitza: 'עַל יְדֵי הָאֲנָחָה, הוּא מְחַיֶּה וּמַבְרִיא אֶת הָרוּחַ הַדּוֹפֵק' (line 76) — through sighing one heals the pulse. This is a causal/eitza relationship, not a bechina identity. No new bechina node.

Line 27 and 41: 'אֲרִיכוּת יָמִים... שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת דַּעַת.' The longevity/length-of-days is described as a bechina of daat. However, 'אריכות ימים' in this Torah operates as an eitza-bridge concept (Torah → length of days → daat → ability to rebuke) rather than as a standalone bechina node. The concept 'ימים' is already in the dataset (edge 1358: מדות ↔ ימים) and belongs to Package 5. Adding 'אריכות ימים' as a separate node that is bechina of daat would create redundancy with the ימים/מדות cluster. Excluded pending review.
